meaning: The number 42,360 is the total count of Israelites who returned from the Babylonian exile, as described in Ezra 2:64 and Nehemiah 7:66.
description: This number symbolizes God's faithfulness to his people and the fulfillment of prophecies that Israel would be restored after exile. It represents the community's reunification and their collective return to the promised land after 70 years of captivity in Babylon, in line with Jeremiah's prophecy (Jer 25:11–12). In Jewish tradition, this return is seen as a sign of God's covenant with his people and his promise of restoration. The number marks the beginning of the Second Temple period, when the people gathered to rebuild the temple and renew worship in Jerusalem.

It is acceptable as a theological reference, though it could be clarified.; [minor] It could be useful to have a footnote mentioning the well-known discrepancy between the total figure of 42,360 and the sum of the individual groups listed in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7, since these do not match. footnotes.text: The sum of the individual groups listed in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 does not match the total figure of 42,360. In Ezra 2, adding up the individual groups gives approximately 29,818, while in Nehemiah 7 it is about 31,089. The discrepancy has been widely discussed among biblical scholars and may be due to certain groups (such as women, children, or individuals with uncertain tribal affiliation) being included in the total but not in the individual listings.

The return was made possible by the decree of Persian King Cyrus II in 538 BC, which allowed the Jewish exiles to return to Judah and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem (Ezra 1:1–4). This decree is also known from the archaeological Cyrus Cylinder.

The 70 years in Babylon are traditionally counted from the destruction of the First Temple in 586 BC to the dedication of the Second Temple in 516 BC, although other calculations exist in rabbinic literature.
